gates.title: SEED-STABILITY: stations whose two-seed count split is inside the alpha=0.05 band (window-native GEH < 2.7718)

reference.cite: tools/sumo_realism.py SEED_STABILITY_BASIS (derived; NOT an external standard and NOT the FHWA criteria)
reference.source: Exact conditional null for two runs of the SAME scenario with different RNG seeds: at a station the two runs record m and c vehicles over the same window; conditional on the total n = m + c, an unbiased split gives m ~ Binomial(n, 1/2), so (m - c)/sqrt(n) ~ N(0,1) and the window-native GEH = sqrt(2*(m-c)^2/(m+c)) = sqrt(2) * |Z| exactly. A per-station GEH bound is therefore a two-sided z-test with a known false-alarm rate, and the bounds below are quoted as such. These are derived thresholds local to tools/sumo_realism.py; they are NOT an external standard and are deliberately NOT the FHWA criteria. Bound 2.7718 = sqrt(2)*z_(1-alpha/2) at alpha=0.05, so under the null each station fails with probability 0.05; requiring 0.85 of N stations leaves a small documented false-alarm budget (~1.5% at N=22). This is 1.80x tighter than the FHWA GEH < 5 link bound ON THE SAME WINDOW-NATIVE SCALE.

gates.title: SEED-STABILITY: worst station's window-native GEH (Bonferroni family-wise alpha=0.05 over N stations)

reference.cite: tools/sumo_realism.py SEED_STABILITY_BASIS (derived; NOT an external standard and NOT the FHWA criteria)
reference.source: Exact conditional null for two runs of the SAME scenario with different RNG seeds: at a station the two runs record m and c vehicles over the same window; conditional on the total n = m + c, an unbiased split gives m ~ Binomial(n, 1/2), so (m - c)/sqrt(n) ~ N(0,1) and the window-native GEH = sqrt(2*(m-c)^2/(m+c)) = sqrt(2) * |Z| exactly. Bound 4.3163 = sqrt(2)*z_(1-alpha/(2N)) with alpha=0.05 and N=22: under the null the WHOLE gate raises a false alarm with probability <= 0.05. This is the gate that catches a change localised to one loop.

gates.title: SEED-STABILITY: relative difference of the network-total loop count

reference.cite: tools/sumo_realism.py SEED_STABILITY_BASIS (derived; NOT an external standard and NOT the FHWA criteria)
reference.source: Exact conditional null for two runs of the SAME scenario with different RNG seeds: at a station the two runs record m and c vehicles over the same window; conditional on the total n = m + c, an unbiased split gives m ~ Binomial(n, 1/2), so (m - c)/sqrt(n) ~ N(0,1) and the window-native GEH = sqrt(2*(m-c)^2/(m+c)) = sqrt(2) * |Z| exactly. A per-station GEH bound is therefore a two-sided z-test with a known false-alarm rate, and the bounds below are quoted as such. These are derived thresholds local to tools/sumo_realism.py; they are NOT an external standard and are deliberately NOT the FHWA criteria. 0.03 vs the 0.05 FHWA VALIDATION allows: demand is a fixed route file, so the network-wide loop total is not free to drift with the seed -- only crossing times shift. The 0.6 ratio mirrors FHWA's own calibration-to-validation tightening (GEH 3 vs 5).

gates.title: SEED-STABILITY: stations inside the per-station count band |delta| <= max(3 veh, 0.25*max(m,c))

reference.cite: tools/sumo_realism.py SEED_STABILITY_BASIS (derived; NOT an external standard and NOT the FHWA criteria)
reference.source: Exact conditional null for two runs of the SAME scenario with different RNG seeds: at a station the two runs record m and c vehicles over the same window; conditional on the total n = m + c, an unbiased split gives m ~ Binomial(n, 1/2), so (m - c)/sqrt(n) ~ N(0,1) and the window-native GEH = sqrt(2*(m-c)^2/(m+c)) = sqrt(2) * |Z| exactly. A per-station GEH bound is therefore a two-sided z-test with a known false-alarm rate, and the bounds below are quoted as such. These are derived thresholds local to tools/sumo_realism.py; they are NOT an external standard and are deliberately NOT the FHWA criteria. An ENGINEERING equivalence bound, complementary to the z-calibrated GEH gate: a relative-only tolerance is meaningless at 1-3 vehicles, hence the absolute floor. Every station in this layout sits in FHWA's below_700 band, whose tolerance is +-100 veh/h (= +-8.33 vehicles over this window), so the band is far tighter than FHWA's. The required pass rate is 0.8 rather than 0.85 because pure counting noise at these station counts (~+-30% at 10 vehicles) already pushes some stations outside the band; the gate targets a systematic drift that moves many stations together, not per-station equality.
